Only one CH3 suggests maybe a methyl attached to carbonyl (acetyl) and rest is unsaturated chain with O maybe as alcohol.

C11H14O2 DBE 5. DBE formula: DBE = C - H/2 + N/2 +1 = 11 -14/2 +1 = 11 -7 +1 =5. Good. Aromatic ring contributes 4 DBE (benzene ring = 4). Carbonyl adds 1 DBE. So total 5 matches. So the rest of structure is saturated (no extra double bonds). So we have benzene ring (6 C) + carbonyl (C=O) attached to something else (maybe an alkyl chain). The carbonyl is part of a ketone or aldehyde attached to aromatic ring. Since only one carbonyl, likely a phenyl ketone: Ar-CO-R. The DBE accounted for carbonyl. So carbonyl carbon is part of the ester, O attached to propyl. Count: phenyl C6, carbonyl C1 =7, propyl C3 =10. That's C10, not C11. Hmm.

Our formula C11 suggests propyl chain of 4 carbons? Phenyl butanoate: phenyl-CO-O-CH2CH2CH2CH3 gives C11. Yes phenyl butanoate (phenyl butyrate). So aliphatic carbons: carbonyl carbon (C=O) and methyl carbon (CH3). That's 2. So total unique = aromatic 5 + carbonyl C (1) + methyl C (1) =7. Not 8.
